clue.text: Practice of biltong eaters died in invention of 11 dish

parts.note: biltong is a South African dried meat, so its eaters are South Africans, SA
a usage is a customary practice

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation for died inside the rearranged letters
an invention is something made up afresh, so the letters of 11's answer are recast

parts.note: the answer to 11 across, a leafy vegetable
D is the standard abbreviation for died, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: A South African eating habit turns up inside a dish invented from leafy greens.
explanation.walkthrough: Biltong is South African dried meat, so its eaters are South Africans (SA). 'invention of' rearranges the answer to 11 across, and 'in' slips D inside the result.
explanation.definitionFit: Sausage and chips is a classic British fried meal served in chip shops and cafés.

clue.text: Spot not half, double the dog!

indicators.note: only half of the word Spot is kept, its first two letters

parts.note: a ringer is a person who looks exactly like another, a double

explanation.surface: An exclamation at seeing a spotted dog's lookalike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not half' keeps the front half of Spot, SP, then a dead ringer is a double.
explanation.definitionFit: A springer is a spaniel breed, so it is a kind of dog.

clue.text: One enthralled by conventional chord

indicators.note: being enthralled by something is being held within its grip, so one goes inside

parts.note: trad is short for traditional, conventional
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone captivated by an ordinary musical chord.
explanation.definitionFit: A triad is a three-note chord built from a root, third and fifth.

clue.text: Capital city in county right under one's nose?

parts.note: a tash, short for moustache, grows directly beneath the nose
Kent is an English county in the south-east

explanation.surface: Asks whether a capital lies in a county, right under your nose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right under one's nose' sounds like 'obvious', but literally describes a moustache, informally a tash in Britain. KENT is a county in south-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: Tashkent is the capital of Uzbekistan, a city in Central Asia.

clue.text: Number theorem ends in stunt, as mathematician

indicators.note: in places those two closing letters within the word for a stunt

parts.note: a feat is a daring stunt or exploit

indicators.note: the closing letters of the words Number and theorem are taken

explanation.surface: A theorem in number theory finishes as a stunt, credited to a mathematician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ends' takes R and M, the last letters of Number and theorem, and 'in' puts them inside FEAT. The surface nods to Fermat's Last Theorem.
explanation.definitionFit: Pierre de Fermat was a 17th-century French mathematician famous for number theory.

clue.text: Point made another way

indicators.note: the letters of another are made into something new, rearranged

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: A point argued in a different manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made' signals that the word another is rearranged; 'Point' means a compass point, not an argument.
explanation.definitionFit: North-east is one of the compass points, midway between north and east.

clue.text: Nero's tutor offering brief kiss in the main

indicators.note: in places the shortened kiss inside the sea

parts.note: the main is an old poetic word for the open sea

indicators.note: brief means cut short, so the word for kiss loses its final letter

parts.note: to neck is to kiss amorously

explanation.surface: The emperor's teacher gives a quick peck out at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brief' drops the final letter of the kiss, and 'in' puts what remains inside 'the main', an old poetic term for the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The Stoic philosopher Seneca was tutor and later adviser to the young emperor Nero.

clue.text: Jerk from Ikea has lock to screw up

indicators.note: to jerk is to wrench sharply, so the letters that follow are jolted into a new order

explanation.surface: An idiot from the furniture store has botched a lock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jerk' looks like an insult (the idiot) but is the anagram signal for FROM IKEA HAS LOCK. Horlicks is a British malted drink; making a Horlicks of something is British slang for botching it.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom is British slang for making a mess of a task, bungling it badly.

clue.text: A corresponding housing area that's sweet

indicators.note: housing means holding inside, so one word goes within the other

parts.note: corresponding means matching, the same
a part is a region or area, as in parts of the country

explanation.surface: A matching housing estate turns out to be sugary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'housing' is the containment signal, not homes; 'sweet' is a noun here, a sweetening substance.
explanation.definitionFit: Aspartame is an artificial sweetener, so it is used here as a sweet substance.

clue.text: Jumbo's end jumbo's end!

indicators.note: the end of the word Jumbo gives its final letter

parts.note: jumbo means huge, mega

explanation.surface: An exclamation that the elephant has died, twice over.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'Jumbo's end' is its last letter, O; the second 'jumbo' is MEGA, with 's as 'is' before the definition 'end'.
explanation.definitionFit: Omega is the last letter of the Greek alphabet, hence the final point or end.

clue.text: Reel composer, heading off, leaves

parts.note: to reel is to whirl round, to spin

indicators.note: with its heading off, the composer's name loses its first letter

parts.note: Bach is the German baroque composer

explanation.surface: A dancing composer, leading the way, walks out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading off' drops B from BACH to leave ACH. 'leaves' looks like a verb but is the plural noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Spinach is eaten for its green leaves, a leafy vegetable.

clue.text: See 18
Musical soldiers

parts.note: a GI is an American soldier
the plural gives a second GI, another American soldier

explanation.surface: A show about troops.
explanation.walkthrough: The plural 'soldiers' supplies two GIs side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Gigi is a Lerner and Loewe stage and film musical from the 1950s.

clue.text: Wood with incense right for skin condition

parts.note: to incense is to anger, to nettle
ash is a tree and its timber, a wood

explanation.surface: Timber, perfumed smoke and rightness combine for a dermatological complaint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'incense' looks like the fragrant smoke but is the verb, to anger.
explanation.definitionFit: Nettle rash is urticaria, an itchy rash on the skin like that from stinging plants.

clue.text: Not seen in public once ale downed

indicators.note: in signals that the letters sit inside the run of words public once ale downed

explanation.surface: Drinking ale in public, once downed, went unnoticed.
explanation.definitionFit: Something concealed is hidden away and so unseen.

clue.text: Song left for John Lennon, perhaps

parts.note: an air is a tune or song
port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: A song exchanged for one by John Lennon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'John Lennon' suggests the musician, but here it names Liverpool John Lennon Airport.
explanation.definitionFit: Liverpool's John Lennon Airport is an example of an airfield named after a person.

clue.text: Easy in gold and bronze positions, one speaking as a trier

indicators.note: gold and bronze are first and third places, so the first and third letters of Easy are taken

parts.note: a sayer is one who says something, a speaker

explanation.surface: An easy podium finish for a speaker who keeps trying.
explanation.walkthrough: Medal places: gold is first and bronze third, so 'in gold and bronze positions' takes letters 1 and 3 of Easy, E and S.
explanation.definitionFit: An essayer is one who essays, meaning attempts something, so a person who tries.

clue.text: Minister in eastern capital travelling north, always

indicators.note: in a down clue, travelling north means reading upwards, so the letters run backwards
in places the minister inside the capital

parts.note: Rome is the capital of Italy
Rev, short for Reverend, is the title of a minister of religion

explanation.surface: A clergyman in an eastern capital heading north for good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts the minister inside the Italian capital, E goes in front, and 'travelling north' reads the whole lot upwards, as this is a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Evermore is a literary word for forever, at all times.

clue.text: I don't know the answer that's in vogue, yet theorem fashionable

indicators.note: fashionable is read as fashioned, made into a new shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A confession of ignorance about which theorem is in vogue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fashionable' looks like a partner for 'in vogue', but signals that VOGUE YET THEOREM is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a conversational admission of being stumped by a question.

clue.text: Clever man, butcher slices bird

parts.note: a clever dick is a know-all, so dick is the clever man

indicators.note: to butcher is to hack apart, so the letters of slices are chopped into a new order

explanation.surface: A smart fellow, a butcher who cuts up poultry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'butcher' rearranges SLICES into CISSEL. A clever dick is British slang for a smart alec.
explanation.definitionFit: The dickcissel is a small American bunting-like songbird of the prairies.

clue.text: Out of one's tree one flies

definitions.meaning: a bird is one that flies, as in the novel title about the nest

explanation.definitionFit: Cuckoo means crazy, and the cuckoo is also a well-known bird that lays eggs in other nests.

clue.text: Second drink well hot

parts.note: tea is a drink
my is an exclamation of surprise, like well

explanation.surface: A second drink, well, it's hot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'well' is an exclamation, as is 'my!'.
explanation.definitionFit: Steamy describes something humid and very warm, or full of passion.

clue.text: Car check unfinished

indicators.note: unfinished means the last letter is missing from the word for check

parts.note: an audit is an official check of accounts

explanation.surface: A car inspection left incomplete.
explanation.definitionFit: Audi is a German make of motor car.

clue.text: Thus I depart after initially turning up — toodle-oo!

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up reverses the letters to read upwards

parts.note: so means thus, in this way

indicators.note: initially takes the first letters of depart and after

explanation.surface: Someone says goodbye, leaving after showing up.
explanation.walkthrough: SO, I, D and A make SOIDA, which 'turning up' reverses.
explanation.definitionFit: Adios is Spanish for goodbye, just as toodle-oo is a jaunty farewell.

clue.text: Measure of land close to allotment in concern for men?

indicators.note: in places that closing letter inside the concern

parts.note: a concern for males is playfully a he-care, he standing for a man

indicators.note: close to means the closing letter of allotment

explanation.surface: An acre-style measure near a garden plot, made by worry about men.
explanation.walkthrough: 'close to allotment' gives T, which 'in' places inside HE CARE.
explanation.definitionFit: A hectare is a metric unit of area, 10,000 square metres, used for fields.

clue.text: Wed, married, I had wife — yikes!

parts.note: I'd is the contraction of I had
eek is a cry of alarm, like yikes

explanation.surface: Someone recalls getting married and being alarmed at having a wife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wed' looks like the verb to marry, but is short for Wednesday.
explanation.definitionFit: Wednesday, abbreviated Wed, falls in the middle of the working week.

clue.text: Source of communication that's acidic?

parts.note: a calling device read as a chemistry reading: acidity measured at value one on the scale

explanation.surface: Asks whether a means of contact is sour.
explanation.walkthrough: pH measures acidity, and a pH of 1 is strongly acidic, so the device can be read as pH 1.
explanation.definitionFit: A telephone is a device through which people talk at a distance.

clue.text: Besmirch business, VW, in The Merchant of Venice

parts.note: to besmirch is to spoil or mar
Co is the abbreviation for company, a business
the Polo is a Volkswagen car model

explanation.surface: Smearing a firm and a VW in Shakespeare's play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Merchant of Venice' suggests the Shakespeare play but describes the Venetian trader.
explanation.definitionFit: Marco Polo was a Venetian merchant and traveller who journeyed to China.
